_note: Real south-polar landings replayed through HORIZON. Coordinates, times and outcomes are from the cited sources (read 2026-10-31). Event times marked date_only are known to the day, not the hour. Each replay starts at the landing hour and runs for `days`.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-3 · Vikram
missions.outcome: Worked through one lunar day near 69°S, was put to sleep ahead of the lunar night, and never woke up.

events.label: Put to sleep ahead of lunar night
Wake-up attempt at sunrise: no signal

missions.name: IM-1 · Odysseus
missions.outcome: Tipped onto its side on a 12° slope near Malapert A, worked for about a week, and fell silent on 29 February as the Sun sank toward the horizon. It was not built to survive the night.

missions.name: IM-2 · Athena
missions.outcome: Came down on its side inside a 20 m crater near Mons Mouton. With the Sun this low, its panels could not recharge and the batteries ran down in about 13 hours.

sources.label: Resting place in a 20 m crater (NASA LROC)
Mission end: Sun direction, panels, cold
